title: Why does thunder boom?
examples: Teacher, why does thunder sound so loud?
How does the air help make the boom?

explain.say: Lightning makes the air very hot very fast.
This quick heating makes the air push out with force.
The fast push of air is what we hear as a loud bang.
When lightning happens, it heats the air very quickly.
When you see lightning you will hear thunder soon after.
A fun fact is that sound needs air to travel to your ears.

faq.q: Why is the sound so loud?
faq.a: The sound is loud because the air is pushed out very quickly by the heat.
asks: What makes the thunder sound so big?
Is the boom from the lightning itself?

faq.q: Does the lightning make the thunder?
faq.a: Yes, the lightning causes the air to heat up and expand, making the thunder sound.
asks: Is the thunder just the sound of the lightning?
What is the connection between lightning and thunder?

faq.q: How fast does the sound travel?
faq.a: Sound travels at a speed that is much slower than the light from lightning.
asks: Will the thunder always come after the flash?
How long does it take for the sound to reach me?

faq.q: Does the air have to be hot to make thunder?
faq.a: Yes, the air must get very hot very fast for the rapid expansion to create thunder.
asks: Is heat needed for the boom?
What makes the air expand so much?

faq.q: Can I see the sound of thunder?
faq.a: No, you can only see the light from lightning, not the sound of thunder.
asks: What do I see during a storm?

facts: Lightning heats the air to extremely high temperatures.
This rapid heating causes the air to expand very quickly.
The sudden expansion of air creates a loud sound wave.
This sound wave is what we hear as thunder.

quiz.say: Lightning heats the air very quickly, causing it to expand.

options.show: Raindrops hitting the ground make it.
options.say: Raindrops hitting the ground make it.

options.show: The wind blowing hard makes it.
options.say: The wind blowing hard makes it.

quiz.why: The rapid heating causes the air to push out, making a sound.

wrong.0: This is wrong because raindrops do not heat the air enough to make a loud boom.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the shaking is not the main cause of the loud sound.
wrong.2: This is wrong because wind alone does not create the sudden, powerful pressure change needed.

quiz.say: What is the main process that creates the sound of thunder?

options.show: The water in the clouds making the sound.
options.say: The water in the clouds making the sound.

options.show: The ground shaking from the storm making it.
options.say: The ground shaking from the storm making it.

options.show: The lightning bolt itself makes the sound.
options.say: The lightning bolt itself makes the sound.

quiz.why: The sudden, fast expansion of the hot air creates the sound wave.

wrong.0: The water vapor is not the source of the loud, booming sound.
wrong.1: The ground shaking is not the direct cause of the thunder sound.
wrong.3: The lightning bolt is light, but the sound comes from the air around it.

quiz.say: If you hear thunder, what just happened?
quiz.why: Hearing thunder means the lightning flash happened moments before.

wrong.0: While it means a storm is active, it is not the direct cause of the sound.
wrong.1: The direction of the clouds does not create the sound.
wrong.2: Darkness is a sign of a storm, but not the cause of the boom.
